problem.explanation: A scalar subquery calculates one AVG(salary) value. The outer query compares every employee with it, then sorts qualifying rows. A common mistake is grouping by employee, which calculates many averages instead of one. A CTE containing the average is an equally readable alternative.
hints: First calculate one average for the whole employees table.
Use that scalar result inside the outer WHERE condition.
problem.reference_solution: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees) ORDER BY salary DESC
problem.statement_markdown: Return each employee name and salary when the salary is higher than the average salary across all employees. Sort highest salary first.
problem.title: Employees above average salary
